title: BGN as published: the baseline economy, one priced market shock at a constant price
question: What do the estimators find in the unmodified Berk-Green-Naik economy, measured as every current row is: ten seeds, the current code, the fair benchmark?
notes:
A1 (docs/NEXTUP.md; docs/RESULTS.md, 'Baselines: the anchor'). Every path in RESULTS.md is a departure from one of three baseline economies, and until this spec the only record of this one was a single pre-refactor seed. This spec makes the baseline a first-class economy: ten seeds, the current code, the same protocol as every current row, and the fair linear benchmark (finding 8), so that 'what the route added' is measured against a number produced the same way.

THE ECONOMY: variants/bgn_gam at unit regime multipliers, gmult [1, 1]. The regime chain still runs but both states price the market shock at the paper's sigma_z = 0.4, so the two regime value bases coincide and J0 = J1. REPORT.md section 13e: with the J* table held fixed, bgn_gam at gmult [1, 1] reproduces the baseline bgn economy to machine precision (prices 6e-16, conditional mu 1e-13, Sigma 7e-13 relative) and is regime-path-independent to 1e-14. The calibration is Table I of the paper, 11 of 11 parameters (checked 2026-09-07); the switch probabilities keep their defaults (0.25/12, 0.50/12) and are inert. Own J* table, Jstar_bgnbase.csv: the file name is the solve's tag.

FEATURE COLUMNS (estimation.rf_cols): rf_stand only, the standardised short rate, which is the paper's own state; gam_stand, the regime indicator, is dropped because at unit multipliers it is an unpriced Markov chain unrelated to anything. Every economy exports its full conditioning set into the panel; a baseline drops the columns the paper's model does not have, so that a noise column is not interacted into every basis. The seed array passes it as --rf_cols to run_oracle.py and run_estimators.py, and the oracle summary and the run record carry it.

WHAT THE LEGACY ROW SAID (single seed, same economy, 23f9380:variants/results/grid_summary.csv): SR_max 0.2926, linear ceiling 0.2347, nonlinear ceiling 0.2712, room +0.0365 (all-month), FMR 0.2198, FF 0.2202, best linear 0.2334, DKKM 0.2393, gap +0.0059, t 14.0.

PREDICTION (2026-09-14): room_all +0.030 to +0.045 (the legacy +0.0365 is one draw of this economy); SR_max over the evaluation months 0.25 to 0.35; measured gap +0.000 to +0.015; fair gap within +-0.005 of zero, with mkt_est or linrank_m the fair winner in most seeds, as in every BGN economy. FALSIFIED as a no-gap baseline if the ten-seed fair gap exceeds +0.01: that would mean the unmodified model already carries a complexity gap and every 'what the route added' statement in RESULTS.md is mis-anchored.

PRECOMMITMENT: the jstar id was computed from these parameters and the current source WITHOUT solving (_scratch/precommit_id.sh bgn, which stops rebuild_jstar_gam.py at its solve_id line), and this spec is committed before the table is built. The table is built on the Mac (4 to 8 min) and committed with its manifest, as every BGN J* table is.

changes: the root of bgn_gam Path 1: var-bgn_gam-g0235-v2 is this economy with gmult [0.2, 3.5]

method.bgn_price_of_risk: constant: sigma_z 0.4 in both regimes (gmult [1, 1]), the paper's kernel

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the pre-2026-09-07 single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the old fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
